candidate_guideline_text: XXE / external XML resource resolution: Trace externally supplied XML, SOAP, or XML report/configuration bytes into the exact parser, schema, transformer, or SOAP utility instance. Report only when that instance can process a DOCTYPE, external general or parameter entity, external DTD, schema, or stylesheet without a blocking configuration or resolver. Verify the missing guard on the same source-to-sink path. Remediate by rejecting DOCTYPE where feasible, disabling external entity and external-DTD loading, restricting external-access properties, and installing a resolver that denies external resource resolution before parsing.
evidence_notes: Allure has direct source-backed evidence: default DocumentBuilderFactory/DocumentBuilder parses result files without an EntityResolver or external-entity restriction.

Bonita, DBeaver, and aXMLRPC are plausibly XXE-aligned from their CWE-611 labels and XML utility/parser hunks, but the payload does not show the actual parser settings or attacker-controlled input path.

The AWS Android case is explicitly only a compact review-entry retrieval label, not exploit or mechanism proof; it should not substantiate external-resource resolution without inspecting the patch/source semantics.

The changedetection.io case is labeled template_expression_injection and described as an XPath evaluator issue; the supplied evidence does not establish DTD/entity resolution, so it should be separately evidenced or moved to an expression-injection subgroup.
Fediz and Archi provide only hunk locations with no trace evidence; their fit cannot be confirmed from this payload.
main_issue: The core XXE mechanism is coherent and well described, but the assigned set is explicitly mixed: several cases lack source-level evidence of external-entity resolution, while XPath-expression handling and other XML-related validation/deserialization issues do not necessarily share the same parser-resolution sink or safe fix.
mechanism_name: unsafe XML parser external entity or DTD resolution
split_suggestions: Unsafe XML parser external-resource resolution: default or incompletely hardened DOM/SAX/StAX/JAXB/SOAP parser configuration permits DTD or external entity/resource resolution.

XPath or XML expression injection and XML input-validation issues: attacker-controlled XPath/CSS-JSON expressions, XML names, substitutions, or other expression syntax reach an evaluator without context-appropriate validation or constrained evaluation.
Unsafe XML object deserialization or XML library dependency issues: XMLDecoder/object reconstruction or vulnerable third-party XML component usage, with distinct sinks and remediation.

candidate_guideline_text: Audit Java code that constructs a temporary directory by creating a temporary file, deleting it, and then calling mkdir or mkdirs on the released pathname. In a shared or attacker-influenced filesystem location, an attacker may pre-create or replace the path during that interval, redirecting subsequent writes or use. Prefer Files.createTempDirectory or another atomic directory-creation primitive, and ensure later sensitive operations use the atomically created object.
evidence_notes: CVE-2022-4817, CVE-2018-25068, CVE-2022-3969, and CVE-2021-21363 explicitly document create-temp-file, delete, then mkdir behavior and a Files.createTempDirectory fix.

CVE-2013-2035 supports a related temporary-native-library lifecycle race, but the supplied evidence does not establish the exact create-delete-mkdir sequence; it may need a broader temp-resource race group or separate review.

CVE-2020-15250, CVE-2022-3952, and CVE-2022-41946 provide only source-ready/anchor provenance. Their file_permission_temp_resource labels do not establish a released-path TOCTOU source, sink, or matching atomic-directory fix.
The cluster summary mixes symlink/TOCTOU and overly permissive temporary-resource permissions, which have different missing guards, attacker preconditions, and remediations.
The guideline says it is derived from 10 historical examples while the payload supplies 8 assigned cases; reconcile the provenance count before release.
main_issue: The createTempFile-delete-mkdir TOCTOU mechanism is well supported for five cases, but three file_permission_temp_resource cases have no evidence of that sequence and may instead concern insecure temporary-file permissions or sensitive-data exposure.
mechanism_name: temporary directory create-delete-mkdir TOCTOU race
split_suggestions: Temporary directory create-delete-mkdir TOCTOU: create a temp file, delete it, then recreate the same pathname as a directory before writing or loading sensitive content.
Temporary resource permission exposure: temporary files or directories containing sensitive data are created with overly broad/default permissions, or permission-setting failures are ignored.

Prefer atomic exclusive creation in a securely created private temporary directory, and revalidate containment and file type immediately before the sensitive write when required.

candidate_guideline_text: Trace attacker-influenced URL or endpoint values from API, plugin, configuration, webhook, callback, or bridge inputs into outbound HTTP request construction and dispatch. Review whether the HTTP client receives the same host and scheme that the security policy parsed and validated. Require destination controls that reject disallowed schemes and private, loopback, link-local, multicast, unique-local, and cloud-metadata addresses after resolution; apply equivalent checks to redirects and prevent DNS or parser inconsistencies from bypassing the decision. Report only when an untrusted or insufficiently constrained destination can reach the outbound request path.
evidence_notes: CVE-2026-10662 concretely shows caller-controlled zip_file_url forwarded through an MCP-to-Blender bridge and fetched with requests.get after only an http(s) prefix check.
CVE-2026-44502 supports a distinct parser/client disagreement variant: urlparse-derived hostname policy can differ from the requests/urllib3 request destination.
CVE-2023-37262 supports incomplete private-address classification in an outbound-destination predicate, including metadata, multicast, and IPv6 coverage.

The Backstage, Budibase, Chartbrew, Junoclaw, and prompts.chat entries state that their spans are retrieval review-entry ground truth, explicitly not exploit proof; they do not independently establish webhook/callback URL-to-request paths.
The cluster summary includes TLS, credential, authorization, ReDoS, and race-condition issues, which should not be used to broaden this SSRF guideline without case-level mechanism evidence.
main_issue: The concrete cases support attacker-influenced outbound URL handling and incomplete destination policy enforcement, but the group is over-scoped as webhook/callback fetching and several listed cases provide only retrieval-anchor provenance rather than source-to-sink mechanism evidence.
mechanism_name: attacker-controlled webhook or callback URL fetch

candidate_guideline_text: Trace attacker-controlled URL parameters and stored-but-user-supplied resource URLs into server-side URL.openStream, URLConnection, HTTP clients, download helpers, proxy clients, and redirect-following fetch routines. Review whether the exact source-to-sink path restricts allowed schemes, validates the effective destination host and resolved IP address, blocks loopback/private/link-local/metadata targets, and revalidates every redirect target before the request is made. A safe fix applies these controls before the outbound connection on the same path.

candidate_guideline_text: During archive extraction or import, trace each attacker-controlled entry name through destination-path construction to the filesystem write, link, directory-creation, metadata, or deletion operation. Resolve the entry against the intended extraction root; normalize path separators and canonical or real paths as appropriate; then enforce containment under that root immediately before the sensitive operation. Review string-prefix checks, mixed slash/backslash inputs, absolute paths, drive-qualified paths, and pre-existing or newly created symlinks. A safe fix rejects entries whose resolved target escapes the extraction root and applies the containment check on the exact path used by the sink.
evidence_notes: TestNG CVE-2022-4065 has a direct JarEntry name -> new File(tempDir, entryName) -> copyFile flow with no normalized destination containment check.
Plexus Archiver CVE-2018-1002200 resolves archive entryName directly, then creates directories, symlinks, or output files without checking that the target remains under the extraction directory.
DSpace CVE-2022-31195 provides an archive-entry extraction path and file-write anchors, but the supplied evidence stops before demonstrating the missing containment check at the exact write sink.
The Alibaba OneAgent, QTIWorks, and Goomph entries are review-entry anchors only; they do not establish the claimed mechanism from the supplied payload.
The MCPMappingViewer and TJWS2 entries provide only hunks and CWE-22 context, so their source shape and sink relationship require verification before they can support the group.
The summary's infinite-loop/cycle variants are a separate mechanism from canonical-path traversal and are not covered by the current guideline.
main_issue: The evidenced cases coherently describe archive-entry path traversal leading to writes outside an extraction root, but the cluster summary also includes distinct infinite-loop/null-cycle failures and several listed cases lack source-to-sink evidence. The guideline should be narrowed to archive extraction and explicitly cover separator normalization and symlink-aware containment.
mechanism_name: path traversal through missing canonical prefix check
split_suggestions: Archive-entry traversal and arbitrary file write outside the extraction root
Archive extraction denial of service from cyclic links, null handling, or unbounded extraction loops

candidate_guideline_text: Trace attacker-controlled redirect targets, callback URLs, return URLs, Referer-derived destinations, OAuth/OIDC redirect_uri values, and browser navigation targets into redirect responses, Location headers, response.sendRedirect, window.location assignments, or protocol authorization redirects. Report a path when the final decoded and normalized destination can reach an external or unsafe-scheme target without an exact policy check. Require the guard to validate the final parsed URL on the same source-to-sink path: permit only relative paths resolved against the expected origin, exact registered callback URIs, or explicitly allowlisted scheme/origin/path combinations. Reject prefix-only matching, ambiguous normalization, protocol-relative targets, and non-browser-safe schemes unless explicitly registered.

pybbs redirects a request Referer value, and DSpace redirects callerUrl from the request; both are direct untrusted-destination-to-redirect flows.

Several cases are unrestricted external redirects or weak host/path matching rather than scheme-only bypasses.
mechanism_name: open redirect through unsafe URI scheme validation
